title: Learning Basie had gone to Chicago without him
summary: He, Freddie Green and Ted Donnelly heard the news outside the Hotel Theresa, and he realized how dependent he had been on Basie.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: No, no. In fact, we didn't even know Basie had a small band. Freddie Green and I and the trombone player, Ted Donnelly, we met in front of the Theresa (Hotel) one afternoon and somebody -- somebody not even a musician -- said, man, how come you all are not going to Chicago? I said, "What do you mean?" He said, "Well, Basie just caught a plane going to Chicago to open up in some bar." Not the Carriage Bar, another bar in Chicago. I said, "You've got to be kidding." I couldn't believe it. I said, "He wouldn't do that."

And Freddie Green said, oh, that can't be true. And we found out it was authentic. You know, he'd -- that's when I really became almost hysterical. Because -- after all those years with Basie and not -- you know, it's very easy to be a side

man because you don't have -- the band leader has to get all the work. All you have to do is lean around and get up and play. You just lay around until you get a telephone call that says, well, we're leaving at 4:00 o'clock tomorrow. We'll be out three months. Get your things packed. Because everytime we went out, it was a long trip. You know, you didn't have to worry about working.
But when that -- you become dependent on yourself. Then it creates -- you think and you wonder how you're going to sound without that --
Yeah. Without Basie. I joined Basie when I was a kid, you know, I had been irresponsible all that time. I had depended on him just like I would a father.
